'''Bo Li''' is a Chinese-American statistician whose research focuses on [[spatial statistics]], spatio-temporal statistics, [[geostatistics]], and [[environmental statistics]], with applications in [[paleoclimatology]], estimation of [[crop yield]]s, and agriculture-related cancer risks.{{r|hartley}} She is the Stanley A. Sawyer Professor in the Department of Statistics and Data Science at the [[Washington University in St. Louis]]. {{r|pwashu}} 

==Education and career==
Li studied [[naval architecture]], ocean engineering, [[fluid mechanics]], and industrial foreign trade at [[Shanghai Jiao Tong University]] in China, earning bachelor's and master's degrees there. She went to [[Texas A&M University]] for graduate study in statistics. She earned a second master's degree in 2004, and completed her Ph.D. in 2006{{r|profile}} under the joint supervision of [[Raymond J. Carroll]] and Michael Sherman.{{r|hartley|mg}}

After completing her Ph.D., she was a postdoctoral researcher at the [[National Center for Atmospheric Research]], and then from 2008 to 2013 an assistant professor of statistics at [[Purdue University]]. She moved to the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign in 2013.{{r|hartley}} She was named as a Data Science Founder Professorial Scholar in 2019,{{r|data}} given the Marjorie Roberts Professorship in 2023, {{r|roberts}}, and was the chair of the Department of Statistics from 2019-2024.{{r|chair}} In 2024, she moved to the newly founded Department of Statistics and Data Science at [[Washington University in St. Louis]] as the Stanley A. Sawyer Professor in Statistics and Data Science. {{r|mwashu|pwashu}} 

She is 2023 chair of the American Statistical Association Section on Statistics and Environment,{{r|envr}} and serves on the Advisory Committee on Environmental Research and Education of the [[National Science Foundation]] Office of Integrative Activities.{{r|ace}}

==Recognition==
Li was named as a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]] in 2019.{{r|fasa}} She was the 2020 recipient of the H.O. Hartley Award, given by the Texas A&M University to a former student for distinguished service to statistics.{{r|hartley}} The American Statistical Association Section on Statistics and Environment gave her their Distinguished Achievement Award in 2022.{{r|daa}}
